title: Tuna and White Bean Salad
subtitle: Tinned tuna and cannellini beans with lemon, parsley and olive oil
excerpt: A pantry salad of tinned tuna and cannellini beans dressed in olive oil, lemon juice and flat-leaf parsley. Quick, satisfying, and better the longer it sits.
sourceNotes: Tonno e fagioli (tuna and bean salad) is a classic of Italian antipasto and summer cooking, particularly in Tuscany. The combination of tinned tuna, cannellini beans, red onion and olive oil has been documented in Italian cookbooks since at least the mid-20th century. It is one of the simplest and most versatile pantry salads in the Mediterranean tradition.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be assembled up to 2 hours ahead. The flavour improves as it sits.

content.text: Tuna and white bean salad is what to make when the fridge has nothing interesting in it. Good-quality tinned tuna and a tin of cannellini beans, dressed with olive oil, lemon and red onion, produce a lunch that takes ten minutes and keeps until tomorrow. It is Italian in origin and far better than it has any right to be.

items.prepNote: drained (2 tins, in spring water or olive oil)

content.text: Drain the tuna and beans and tip both into a large bowl. Add the red onion, celery (if using) and most of the parsley. Whisk together {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, the juice of {{lemon}}, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently so the tuna breaks into large flakes rather than crumbs. Scatter the remaining parsley over the top. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Leave for 10 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Tuna or beans not drained thoroughly.
items.fix: Press the drained beans dry with kitchen paper. Drain tinned tuna in a sieve and press gently.

items.cause: Raw red onion has a strong bite.
items.fix: Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain. This removes the harsh raw edge without losing the flavour.

content.text: Tonno e fagioli is a Tuscan summer dish, part of the Italian antipasto tradition. It came to British cooking in the 1980s as Italian ingredients became widely available. It is one of the few salads made entirely from tins and jars.
